The contract contains conditional exclusivity provisions regarding development rights in the Territory. Section 1.1 grants the Developer either non-exclusive or exclusive development rights. If exclusive, Section 1.2 prohibits the Franchisor from granting development rights to others or establishing/franchising restaurants within the Territory without the Developer's prior written consent, provided the Developer is in compliance with the Agreement. However, the Franchisor retains the right to sell similar products through other channels (e.g., grocery stores, internet) and operate restaurants outside the Territory. Additionally, Section 1.1 clarifies that exclusive rights apply only to development, not to territory protection for individual franchise agreements. Section 11.3 allows the Franchisor to terminate or modify these exclusive rights if the Developer defaults.

Section 20.1 of the Development Agreement contains the primary competitive restriction (Covenant Not to Compete) and includes specific exceptions/carveouts that should be reviewed. The exceptions include: 1) The Developer may operate an El Pollo Loco restaurant pursuant to a Franchise Agreement with the Franchisor; 2) The Developer may own less than five percent (5%) of the issued or outstanding stock of any publicly traded company, provided the Developer does not control or become involved in the operations of such company; 3) The Franchisor may consent to the Developer's continued operation of any business already in existence and operating at the time of execution of the Agreement. Additionally, Section 1.2 (applicable to exclusive agreements) outlines rights retained by the Franchisor that act as exceptions to the exclusivity granted to the Developer, allowing the Franchisor to operate outside the Territory, sell products through other channels, and operate non-branded restaurants with similar menus.

Section 13.9, titled 'Bioamber Non-Compete Commitment,' contains a specific non-compete restriction. It prohibits Bioamber from engaging in the development of biocatalysts other than E. coli for the production of succinic acid or salts thereof, except for activities under this Agreement. This restriction applies during the Term of the Development Agreement. Bioamber is permitted to evaluate other biocatalysts but must cease funding and development if a biocatalyst demonstrates the ability to produce succinic acid above a certain concentration. The restriction covers biocatalysts developed in-house, licensed-in, or developed at third-party labs funded by Bioamber.

The contract contains exclusivity-related provisions in two main areas. First, Section 1.2.5 imposes a restriction on Cargill, stating that 'No other party has rights to its services as described in the Work Plan' and that Cargill shall not accept work assignments or conduct work to develop microorganisms for the direct or indirect production of succinic acid during the Term. This acts as an exclusivity commitment regarding Cargill's development services for this specific technology. Second, Section 13.9 contains a 'Bioamber Non-Compete Commitment' which restricts Bioamber from engaging in the development of biocatalysts other than E. coli for the production of succinic acid or salts thereof, except under this Agreement. This effectively creates an exclusive arrangement where Bioamber relies on Cargill's CB1 technology for succinic acid production during the Term, prohibiting collaboration with other parties for alternative biocatalyst development in this field.

Section 13.9 (Bioamber Non-Compete Commitment) contains a non-compete restriction prohibiting Bioamber from developing biocatalysts other than E. coli for succinic acid production. This section includes specific exceptions/carveouts: (1) Bioamber is permitted to evaluate other biocatalysts to identify alternative technologies, provided it does not undertake development; and (2) Bioamber must cease funding and development of any such biocatalyst within 30 days if it demonstrates the ability to produce succinic acid above a certain concentration. Additionally, Section 1.2.5 contains a carveout to Cargill's restriction on developing microorganisms for succinic acid production, allowing Cargill to develop microorganisms for precursors (e.g., fumaric acid, malic acid) so long as they are not converted to succinic acid, and allowing Cargill to sell dextrose to third parties or modify starches for succinic acid derivatives.

The contract contains significant exclusivity provisions that require legal review. Specifically, Section 3.1 grants Integra a 'sole and exclusive worldwide right' to sell and commercialize products using PcoMed's Surface Modification Technology in the defined Field and Territory. This includes a prohibition on PcoMed selling or offering for sale, or granting rights to any Third Party for products utilizing this technology in the Field/Territory. Additionally, Section 3.3 imposes an exclusive coating restriction on Integra, prohibiting the application of any other coating to treated products (except for identification or sterilization). These exclusivity rights are conditional; Section 3.2 allows PcoMed to convert the arrangement to non-exclusive if Integra fails to meet Minimum Payments or other payment obligations. The exclusivity applies during the term of the agreement, and rights cease upon termination (Section 4.4(b)), though a transition period allows for the sale of existing inventory (Section 4.4(c)).

The contract does not contain a standard Most Favored Nation (MFN) clause that grants the buyer the right to receive better terms if offered to a third party. While Section 5.2.2(a) contains a pricing protection provision stating that the price charged to Ginkgo shall be no greater than the lowest price charged to any similarly situated third party, this is a 'most favored customer' pricing parity clause rather than a broad MFN clause covering all terms of the agreement. There is no explicit language stating that if a third party gets better terms on licensing or sale, the buyer is entitled to those better terms generally.

The contract contains specific non-compete and competitive restriction provisions primarily located in Article 6 (Restrictions). 

1. **Headstart Period (Section 6.1.1)**: BLI is restricted from using, practicing, or exploiting 'Headstart Inventions' (developed jointly or by BLI for Ginkgo) during the Headstart Period. Ginkgo has the sole right to use these inventions during this time. This acts as a temporary non-compete on specific IP.

2. **Restrictions on BLI (Section 6.2.1)**: During the Term and for a specified period (redacted, e.g., [***] months) following the Term, BLI is restricted from developing, configuring, customizing, licensing, selling, or providing the Beacon Platform or any [***] to [***] (likely Ginkgo's competitors or specific entities, though redacted) or its Affiliates for any use. This is a direct non-compete restriction on BLI's ability to serve certain parties with the Beacon Platform.

3. **Specific Implementation Restrictions (Section 8.9)**: While BLI is permitted to independently develop workflows similar to 'Specific Implementations' (Independent Development), it is prohibited from using any [***] (likely Ginkgo's Confidential Information or IP) to do so. Using such information to develop competing workflows is deemed a material breach.

These clauses restrict BLI's ability to compete with Ginkgo in specific areas (Headstart Inventions, Beacon Platform provision to certain parties) and restrict the use of Ginkgo's IP for competitive development.

The contract contains specific competitive restriction exceptions in Section 6.1.1 (BLI Standstill) and Section 8.9 (Specific Implementation Restrictions). 

1. Section 6.1.1 provides an exception to the Headstart Period standstill, stating that it does not prevent a Third Party BLI customer or partner from using, practicing, or exploiting any independently developed improvement, invention, process, or workflow, even if similar to a Headstart Invention, provided BLI and its Affiliates comply with the standstill restrictions.

2. Section 8.9 provides an exception to restrictions on Specific Implementations, allowing BLI or its Affiliates to independently develop a Workflow or component that is similar to a Specific Implementation (defined as 'Independent Development'), provided that the Independent Development does not use any Ginkgo Confidential Information and BLI does not use any Ginkgo Confidential Information to develop it.

The contract does not contain any explicit provisions restricting a party from soliciting or hiring employees or contractors from the counterparty. While Section 5.4.1 discusses personnel obligations, including the provision of dedicated FTEs and Key Persons by BLI to Ginkgo, and Section 11.2.1 requires employees to assign inventions, there are no clauses prohibiting the solicitation, hiring, or inducing to leave of the other party's employees or contractors during or after the term of the agreement.

Section 7 (Exclusivity) contains an exclusivity provision where Sabco agrees not to represent or accept as a primary, secondary, or associate sponsor any other company reasonably deemed to be competitive with Prolong products during the term of the Agreement.

Section 3(d) [Exclusivity] contains significant exclusivity commitments. Specifically, Section 3(d)(i) prohibits the Company from entering into agreements with other providers of manifesting or shipping services through non-carrier retail shipping locations, with specific exceptions for carrier drop-boxes and agreements that prohibit the use of the Manifest for retail customers. Section 3(d)(ii) prohibits MBE from entering into agreements with any provider of an online or Internet-based manifest system other than the Company. These exclusivity provisions are subject to termination rights by the Company under Section 3(d)(iii) based on volume or ownership thresholds, and by MBE under Section 3(d)(iv) based on volume and performance issues.

The contract contains specific exceptions to the exclusivity provisions in Section 3(d). 

1. **Exceptions to Company's Exclusivity (Section 3(d)(i))**: The Company is prohibited from entering agreements with other manifest/shipping providers, except:
   - (A) It may provide listings of carrier drop-boxes or carrier-owned counter drop-off locations (excluding retail shipping locations like UPS/FedEx outlets).
   - (B) It may enter such agreements if MBE is given advance written notice, the agreement prohibits using the Manifest/Company Technology for retail customers, and the Company terminates service to any entity that violates this.

2. **Termination of Exclusivity Rights (Section 3(d)(iii) & (iv))**: 
   - The Company may terminate exclusivity if MBE fails to meet shipping volume requirements or ceases to own a certain amount of Company stock.
   - MBE may terminate exclusivity after 18 months if volume requirements are not met due to unsatisfactory Service performance.

3. **Post-Termination Carveout (Section 15(d)(iv))**: After termination, MBE is free to use its personnel or third parties to design, develop, and market an Internet-based manifest system similar to the Manifest (using the Specifications), provided it does not use the object or source code of the Manifest. This acts as an exception to the general IP restrictions and non-compete implications of the exclusivity during the term.

The contract contains specific non-compete and competitive restriction provisions. Section 3(i) restricts Excite@Home from offering any service substantially similar in functionality to the Co-Branded Application during the Term. Section 4(d) and 4(e) restrict both parties from serving advertising for their respective 'Named Competitors' (listed in Exhibit E) on the Co-Branded Application. Section 6(b)(vi) prohibits the Application Provider from soliciting Excite@Home Members on behalf of any Excite@Home Named Competitor during the Term or thereafter. Additionally, Section 16(a)(v) allows Excite@Home to terminate the agreement if the Application Provider is acquired by an Excite@Home Named Competitor.

The contract contains specific restrictions on soliciting customers. Section 6.b.vi explicitly states that the Application Provider (e-centives) 'will not solicit any Excite@Home Member on behalf of any Excite@Home Named Competitor during the Term of this Agreement or thereafter.' Additionally, Section 6.b.i restricts the Application Provider from using Payment-Eligible User Data to 'solicit User traffic to www.e-centives.com or any other co-branded version... with the intent of driving such Users away from using the Co-Branded Application' during the Term. Section 17.b further restricts contact with Users in the event of termination due to acquisition by a Named Competitor.

The contract contains several competitive restriction exceptions and carveouts primarily related to advertising restrictions, data usage, and termination conditions:

1. **Advertising Competitor Exceptions (Section 4.d & 4.e):** Parties may update their list of 'Named Competitors' quarterly, but are explicitly prohibited from adding any company with which the other party has a 'material existing relationship as of the Effective Date.' This carves out existing business relationships from the competitor advertising ban.

2. **Data Usage Exception (Section 6.b.i):** While Application Provider generally cannot use Payment-Eligible User Data to solicit traffic away from the Co-Branded Application, there is a specific exception: 'solely for the period from the Effective Date... to the Launch Date... Application Provider may use Payment Eligible User Data to solicit User traffic to the co-branded area currently in place at http://coupons.excite.com pursuant to the Sponsorship Agreement effective March 5, 1999.'

3. **Data Aggregation Exception (Section 6.b.ii):** Application Provider is prohibited from selling/disclosing identifiable User Data, but there is an exception allowing disclosure if the data is 'aggregated in a non-associatable way with data from multiple online properties or in an anonymous format on a per user basis.'

4. **Termination Exception for Modifications (Section 16.a.vi):** Excite@Home may terminate if Application Provider cannot deliver requested Modifications, but there is an exception: 'Excite shall not be entitled to terminate this Agreement in the event that the requested Modifications exceed or are outside the scope of technology and/or service levels generally available on the Internet.'

5. **Post-Termination Communication Exception (Section 17.a.iii):** In the second post-termination email, Excite@Home may offer a replacement service, creating an exception to the exclusivity of the first email which was 'exclusive to e-centives.'

Section 12 (Exclusivity) contains an exclusive dealing commitment. Charity Tunes agrees that during the period from October 1, 2009, to March 31, 2010, it shall not enable another program sponsorship for all competitive products/product categories distributed/sold within the total Canadian consumer/retail/wholesale marketplace. This includes specific categories such as Total Frozen Handhelds, Total Corporation General Mills Handhelds, Total Pizza Pops Handhelds, and others listed in the section.

The contract contains significant exclusivity provisions that require legal review. Specifically:

1. **Exclusive License Grant**: Section 1(a) grants the Licensee a 'limited, exclusive... right and license' to develop, distribute, and sell Wireless Products based on the Properties for the Wireless Platform in the Territory during the Term. This is an exclusive dealing commitment where Fox grants Licensee the sole right to exploit these specific rights.

2. **Fox's Reservation of Rights (Carveouts)**: Section 1(e)(i) limits this exclusivity by reserving Fox's right to develop or grant rights to third parties for wireless products in Japan. It also states Fox will not grant rights to any 'Licensee Competitor' (defined in Exhibit Q) to develop Wireless Products for the Wireless Platform outside of Japan.

3. **Conditional Exclusivity / Performance Targets**: Section 2(c)(i)(A) states that if Licensee fails to reach specific 'Market Penetration Targets' in Europe, Fox has the right to 'terminate Licensee's exclusivity under this Agreement.' This makes the exclusivity conditional on performance.

4. **Distribution Exclusivity Restrictions**: Section 2(c)(ii) and 2(c)(ii)(A) prohibit Licensee from entering into an 'exclusive distribution agreement with a CSP other than VGSL' in the defined 'VGSL Territories.' This restricts Licensee's ability to grant exclusive distribution rights to third parties in specific regions.

5. **Right of First Negotiation**: Section 4(a) grants Licensee a 'right of first negotiation' for new Major Releases, which acts as a form of preemptive exclusivity for future properties.

Yes, there is a requirement on the Licensee not to disparage the counterparty. Section 13(a)(v)(C) of the Agreement states that the Licensee represents and warrants that it will 'avoid making disparaging, false or misleading statements or representations with regard to Fox, the Property or the Wireless Products.' This is a unilateral obligation on the Licensee to refrain from disparaging Fox.

The contract contains an exclusivity provision in Section 4.2, where the University grants ArTara an 'exclusive license to use the Program Data solely for the Project and in Regulatory Filings in the Field in the Territory.' Additionally, Section 4.3 grants ArTara an 'exclusive Right of Reference' to all Program Regulatory Filings. These clauses restrict the University from licensing the Program Data or Right of Reference to third parties for the specified purposes during the term of the agreement.

The contract contains significant exclusivity provisions. Article 2.1 grants the Licensee (Eurofarma) an 'exclusive, fee-bearing, non-transferable distribution right' and an 'exclusive, royalty-free, non-transferable license' to the Licensor's Patents and Trademarks for the Licensed Product in the Territory. Additionally, Article 2.1(iii) grants an 'exclusive, royalty-bearing, non-transferable license' to the Intellectual Property and Developed Intellectual Property. Article 7 grants an 'exclusive and royalty-free right to use the Trademark in the Territory'. These clauses constitute an exclusive dealing commitment where the Licensor grants exclusive rights to the Licensee, effectively prohibiting the Licensor from licensing or selling the technology/goods to third parties in the Territory during the Term.

The contract contains an exclusivity provision in Section 3, titled 'GRANT OF ENDORSEMENT RIGHTS.' This section grants Teardrop Putter Corporation (TPC) the 'exclusive right and license' to use Brett Ogle's endorsement for the advertisement, promotion, and sale of the Teardrop Putter within the Contract Territory (the entire world) during the Contract Period. Additionally, Section 5 ('RETENTION OF ENDORSEMENT RIGHTS') clarifies the scope of this exclusivity by stating that Consolidated Artists retains the right to license Ogle's endorsement for products other than golf putters, effectively limiting TPC's exclusivity to the specific product category of golf putters.

The contract contains a provision in Section 3(a)(v) that functions similarly to a Most Favored Nation clause regarding pricing. Specifically, VS agrees that it 'shall not... provide preferred pricing to a PPD Competitor which is better than that provided by VS hereunder to PPD.' This ensures PPD receives pricing no less favorable than that offered to competitors. However, there is no explicit clause stating that if a third party gets better terms, PPD is automatically entitled to those better terms (i.e., no automatic price adjustment mechanism is described, only a prohibition on offering better terms to others).

The contract contains significant exclusivity and exclusive dealing commitments in Section 3 (Services Commitment). Specifically:

1. **Exclusivity of Commitments (Section 3(a)(v))**: VS agrees not to enter into the same or substantially similar commitments with any 'PPD Competitor' (companies performing clinical research services similar to PPD) during the Term. Similarly, PPD agrees not to enter into similar commitments with other imaging vendors for Preferred Services. This effectively creates an exclusive relationship for these specific service commitments.

2. **Right of First Refusal (Section 3(a)(v))**: If VS wishes to enter into similar commitments with a PPD Competitor for services outside the Designated Therapeutic Areas, PPD has a 45-day right of first refusal to include those services as 'Preferred Services' under this agreement. This restricts VS's ability to collaborate with competitors in new areas without first offering the opportunity to PPD.

3. **Referral Obligations (Section 3(a)(iv))**: VS must refer opportunities for clinical research services to PPD and cannot refer them to other third-party providers unless PPD declines. PPD must refer opportunities for imaging services (outside the Joint Solution) to VS and cannot refer them to others unless VS declines. This acts as a de facto exclusive sourcing requirement for these referrals.

4. **Recommendation Obligation (Section 3(c))**: PPD agrees to recommend VS to Sponsors when in a position to do so and VS can meet specifications, further reinforcing the exclusive preference.

These provisions restrict both parties from collaborating with competitors on similar services and impose exclusive referral and recommendation duties during the contract term.

Section 21 (Covenant Not to Interfere) contains a restriction on soliciting employees. It states that neither party will solicit for employment any employee of the other party during the active term of the Agreement and the term of any active Work Order. The clause defines 'solicit' as the initiation of contact with current employees performing services under the agreement for the purpose of offering employment, but excludes circumstances where the employee initiates contact in response to general advertisements or third-party contacts not instructed by the hiring party. There is no explicit restriction on soliciting contractors, nor does the restriction explicitly extend to the post-termination period beyond the active Work Orders.

Section 9.0(f) of the Outsourcing Base Agreement contains a restriction on soliciting employees. Specifically, IBM agrees that for a period of [*] years from the Effective Date, it will not solicit for employment any 'Transferred Employees' (employees who moved from IBM to MSL) without the prior written consent of MSL. This restriction includes exceptions for individuals who contact IBM on their own initiative without solicitation, or those hired through general employment advertising or independent search firms, provided IBM does not direct or encourage such firms to solicit Transferred Employees.

No Most Favored Nation clause was found in the contract. The agreement does not contain language granting Liquidmetal the right to receive better terms if Eutectix offers more favorable terms to third parties regarding the licensing or sale of technology/goods/services. Section 2.8 addresses royalties for non-arm's length transactions by comparing prices to 'outside concerns,' but this is a mechanism to prevent under-reporting of sales to affiliates, not an MFN provision granting rights based on third-party deals.

The contract contains restrictions related to competition primarily through the prohibition of unauthorized use of Playboy Properties and the prevention of unfair competition. Specifically, Section 1(iii) prohibits the Supplier from making claims to Playboy Properties or similar marks in connection with the manufacture, advertising, promotion, sale, or distribution of merchandise. Section 2 prohibits the Supplier from producing merchandise using Playboy Properties or similar marks during or after the contract term, except as specifically requested. Section 7 explicitly states that violation may result in prosecution for 'unfair competition.' While these are primarily intellectual property and anti-counterfeiting protections, they function as restrictions on the Supplier's ability to compete using the licensed brand assets.

Section 2.4 (Restrictions on Communications) contains a limited non-compete restriction. It prohibits i-Escrow from running banner advertisements on the Co-Branded Site for any of 2TheMart's competitors. 2TheMart retains the discretion to provide a written list of companies to be excluded from such advertising.

The contract contains specific non-compete and competitive restriction provisions in Article V. Section 5.3 explicitly restricts Moelis Holdings from opening an office in Japan conducting Covered Businesses during the term of the Agreement. Additionally, Section 5.2 includes non-solicitation restrictions regarding clients introduced by the other party, which limits competitive solicitation activities for specific business opportunities involving Japanese Companies in Covered Regions. Section 5.1 also includes a general non-circumvention clause.

Section 5.2 (Non-Solicitation) of the Strategic Alliance Agreement contains a restriction on soliciting customers. Specifically, each party (SMBC/Nikko and Moelis Holdings) agrees not to solicit any 'Client' introduced by the other party in connection with an assignment on Covered Businesses involving Japanese Companies where all principal parties are located within Covered Regions. This restriction applies during the term of the Agreement and for a period of 12 months thereafter. However, there are exceptions: the restriction does not prevent soliciting a Client for purposes other than working on Covered Businesses involving Japanese Companies in Covered Regions, or with Clients with whom the party had a pre-existing relationship prior to the Introduction.

Section 5.2 of the Strategic Alliance Agreement contains the primary competitive restriction (Non-Solicitation of Clients) and includes specific exceptions/carveouts that should be reviewed. The provision restricts soliciting Clients introduced by the other party for Covered Businesses involving Japanese Companies in Covered Regions. However, it explicitly carves out two exceptions: (i) soliciting a Client for any purpose other than working on or obtaining an assignment on Covered Businesses involving Japanese Companies in Covered Regions, and (ii) soliciting a Client with whom the party (or its employees/consultants) has had a pre-existing relationship (including contractual or business relationships) prior to the Introduction of such Client in connection with an assignment covered by the Agreement. Additionally, Section 3.1 notes that the Strategic Alliance is subject to 'pre-existing arrangements of either party,' which serves as a general exception to the scope of cooperation.

Section 5.2 (Non-Solicitation) contains a restriction on soliciting or hiring employees. Specifically, each party (SMBC/Nikko and Moelis Holdings) agrees not to solicit or hire any employee of the other party during the term of the Agreement and for a period of 12 months thereafter. This restriction does not apply to general solicitations to the public that are not specifically directed to employees of the other party.

The contract contains an exclusivity provision in Section 1(a), where AJR designates XC as the 'exclusive technology sponsor' for wearable computer technology of the Team for the Season. This grants XC exclusive rights within that specific category of sponsorship during the term of the agreement.

The contract does not contain an explicit non-disparagement clause. While Section 7 ('Reputation') prohibits AJR from taking actions that could result in an adverse impact on XC's reputation, and Section 6(d) restricts the use of licensed materials to imply endorsement of other sponsors, there is no specific provision requiring either party not to disparage, defame, or make negative statements about the other party.

The contract contains a section titled 'Section 4 Exclusivity', but the text of this section has been redacted and is marked with '[***]'. Consequently, the specific terms regarding exclusive dealing commitments, prohibitions on licensing to third parties, or restrictions on collaborating with other parties are not visible in the provided document. While Section 3.6 grants an 'exclusive' license for joint inventions, this is an IP license provision rather than a general commercial exclusivity or non-compete restriction on the parties' broader business activities. Without the text of Section 4, it is impossible to determine if there are broader exclusivity obligations as defined in the review skill.

No explicit non-disparagement clause was found in the provided contract. While Section 6.3(b) prohibits the Company from tarnishing or bringing into disrepute the reputation of the Seller Licensed Trademarks or Arizona, this is a quality control provision related to trademark usage rather than a general non-disparagement covenant regarding the counterparty itself.

The contract contains significant exclusivity provisions. Section 2.1 appoints the Distributor as the 'exclusive distributor' of the Products in the Territory, subject to Performance Benchmarks. Section 2.3 includes a non-circumvention clause where Hydraspin agrees to deal 'exclusively with and through the Distributor' in the Territory. Additionally, Section 8.1 grants the Distributor an 'exclusive non-transferable and royalty-free right and license to use Hydraspin's Marks' in the Territory. The agreement also provides the Distributor with the first opportunity to become the exclusive distributor for any new territories Hydraspin enters in the United States.

Section 2.2 (Sales Outside the Territory) provides an exception to the exclusivity and non-solicitation restrictions. It allows the Distributor to advertise, promote, market, or solicit customers with a business presence outside the defined Territory, provided that the Distributor does not conduct solicitation activities in any outside territory where Hydraspin is bound to an exclusive distributor agreement with a third party, and only if Hydraspin has notified the Distributor in writing of such arrangements and territories.

Section 8 of the Services Agreement contains a Non-Competition provision. It restricts Maimon from competing with the business of the Company, whether individually or through any entity, during the term of the Agreement and for a period of two (2) years after expiration or termination. It also prohibits using Confidential Information for the purpose of competing with the Company.

answer: Section 8 of the Services Agreement contains a Non-Solicitation provision. Specifically, subsection (b) restricts Maimon from suggesting to, inducing, or persuading any customer, client, vendor, supplier, employee, consultant, or agent of the Company to terminate or diminish their relationship with the Company. This restriction applies during the term of the Agreement and for a period of two (2) years after its expiration or termination.

Section 8 of the Services Agreement contains a non-solicitation provision. Specifically, subsection (b) states that during the term of the Agreement and for two years after expiration or termination, Maimon agrees not to 'suggest to, induce or persuade any... employee, consultant or agent of the Company to terminate or diminish its relationship with the Company.' This constitutes a restriction on soliciting employees and contractors (consultants/agents) both during the contract and after it ends.

Yes, the contract contains an exclusivity commitment. Section 8, titled 'Exclusivity,' explicitly states that during the Term and in the Territory, the Celebrity (Paul Silas) will not endorse or make any appearances or advertisements on behalf of any other multivitamin. This constitutes a prohibition on collaborating with other parties in a specific product category (multivitamins) during the contract term.

The contract contains exclusivity provisions in Article I, Section 1.1 and Section 1.2. Section 1.1 designates the Sponsor as the '[redacted] vitamin and supplement sponsor' and '[redacted] vitamin and supplement advertiser' on the drkoop.com Website throughout the Term. Section 1.2(i) further specifies that the Sponsor shall be the '[redacted] sponsor of the Nutrition Center' and each area within it (excluding specific 'Excluded Areas' related to cooking/food recipes). These clauses establish an exclusive sponsorship arrangement for vitamins and nutritional supplements on the website during the contract term.

Article 14 (NON-COMPETITION AND EXCLUSIVE RIGHTS) contains significant non-compete restrictions. Section 14.1 restricts IMPCO from entering into other Joint Venture or Marketing/Distribution Agreements in the Territory regarding the Products during the Agreement term. Section 14.2(a) restricts MINDA/MIL from entering into similar agreements for goods similar to the Products in the Territory during the term and for five years after termination (if terminated by IMPCO due to default), specifically prohibiting the use of Technical Know-How. Section 14.2(c) includes a severability clause stating that if the time period or geographic scope is deemed unreasonable, the restrictions shall remain in effect for the greatest enforceable period and within the Territory.

The contract contains significant exclusivity and non-competition provisions in Article 14. Specifically, Section 14.1 grants IMPCO exclusive rights by prohibiting it from entering into other Joint Venture or Marketing/Distribution Agreements for the Products in the Territory during the term of the Agreement. Section 14.2 imposes a reciprocal exclusivity/non-compete obligation on MINDA/MIL, prohibiting them from entering into similar agreements for goods similar to the Products in the Territory during the term and for five years after termination (if terminated due to default). Additionally, Article 9.2 restricts the JVC's ability to export Products directly, requiring prior written consent from IMPCO, effectively giving IMPCO exclusive control over exports.

Section 3.3 of the Co-Branding Agreement contains an exclusivity provision. It states that 'During the Term, ebix shall be the exclusive integrated online insurance provider in the Channels and Guide Sites listed in Section 3.1 above.' This constitutes an exclusive dealing commitment where About agrees not to collaborate with other parties for integrated online insurance services within the specified channels during the contract term.

The contract contains a restriction on the Talent's ability to compete in the specific business sector of the endorsed product. Section 7(a) includes a representation and warranty where the Talent agrees that he has not granted, nor will he grant, any right to use his Property in connection with products that are 'identical or substantially similar' to the Company's Product (defined as educational training related to real estate, securities, and options trading). This acts as a non-compete restriction within the specific category of the endorsed product during the term of the agreement. Additionally, Section 6(a) clarifies that the Talent is not prevented from endorsing other products or services that are not substantially similar to the Product, defining the scope of the restriction.

The contract contains significant non-compete restrictions in Section 19 (Covenants). Specifically, Section 19.3 prohibits the Franchisee from owning, operating, or having an interest in any 'Competitive Business' (defined in Section 19.2.2 as any property and/or casualty insurance distribution business) during the term of the Agreement and for two years after expiration or termination. Section 19.4 specifies that during the term, there is no geographical limitation, but post-termination, the restriction applies only within the city and county of the Approved Location. Additionally, Section 19.5 prohibits selling or leasing the Approved Location to anyone intending to operate a Competitive Business for two years post-termination. Section 19.3.2 also includes a no-solicit of employees clause. These provisions should be reviewed by a lawyer to assess enforceability, particularly regarding the scope of 'Competitive Business' and the geographical/temporal limitations.

The contract contains significant 'No-Solicit of Customers' restrictions in Section 19 (Covenants). Specifically, Section 19.3.1 prohibits the Franchisee from diverting or attempting to divert any actual or potential business or customer of any Goosehead Business to a competitor during the term of the Agreement and for two years after termination. Section 19.5.2 explicitly prohibits the Franchisee from soliciting, diverting, or attempting to solicit or divert any actual or potential business or customer of the Franchised Business to any Competitive Business for a period of two years after expiration, non-renewal, termination, or transfer. Additionally, Section 1.4.2 restricts the Franchisee from offering or selling services through means other than the Franchised Business (e.g., satellite locations, mobile vehicles), which limits solicitation channels.

The contract contains specific exceptions to the competitive restrictions (Non-Compete) found in Section 19. Section 19.7 provides an exception for the ownership of less than five percent (5%) beneficial interest in the outstanding equity securities of any publicly-held corporation. Additionally, Section 19.4 states that the restrictions do not apply to businesses that the Franchisor (or its affiliates) has franchised to the Franchisee pursuant to a valid franchise agreement.

Section 19.3.2 of the Franchise Agreement contains a restriction on soliciting or hiring employees. It states that during the term of the Agreement and for two years after expiration or termination, the Franchisee will not 'Employ or seek to employ any person who is then employed by us or any other Goosehead Business franchisee or developer, or otherwise directly or indirectly induce such person to leave his or her employment.' Additionally, Section 6.3.3 requires the Franchisee's Operating Principal, Managers, and Producers to sign personal covenants including non-competition agreements (referenced as Exhibit F), which typically contain similar non-solicit provisions for employees.

The contract contains an exclusivity provision in Section 3, titled 'EXCLUSIVE RIGHTS'.
